text:
alex: quick check — i'm finishing a tiny follow-up to the streaming schema PR. current PR mixes raw text fragments with a separate finalization event and some clients are struggling to reassemble reliably. want consensus on a small shape change.

maria: ping — can you show the minimal example you want to land? :eyes:

alex: sure, here are the two variants floating around:
```json
{ \"event_type\": \"delta\", \"payload\": { \"role\": \"assistant\", \"content\": \"hello\" } }
{ \"event_type\": \"final\", \"payload\": { \"summary\": \"done\" } }
```

alex: proposed unified shape: every stream event has an \"event_type\" and a small set of common metadata so clients can reassemble without special-casing the last message. e.g. add a numeric \"seq\" and an optional \"chunk_index\"/\"chunk_count\" for multi-part chunks.

jing: i like the metadata approach. one ask: avoid duplicating a boolean final + final event_type. prefer explicit types like `delta`, `func_start`, `func_chunk`, `func_end`, `eos`. makes client logic clearer.

owen: operational note — a lot of mobile/edge clients reorder/merge fragments; a monotonic `seq` per-response is the simplest. if seq is optional, older clients can ignore but newer clients will rely on it. can we require `seq` for streaming-only responses and set to 0 for non-streaming?

sam: +1 on seq. also for function calling we should standardize event_types: `function_call:start`, `function_call:update`, `function_call:finish`. function args streaming should use content-type metadata and a `chunk_index`. otherwise clients try to parse partial JSON and fail.

maria: backward-compatibility question: if we add seq and chunk fields, do we auto-fill for older backends? is there vendor migration impact?

alex: plan is to make fields optional but documented as recommended. new runtime will emit them for all streaming responses. we can add a feature-flag header so dedicated/private customers can opt-in while older hosted models keep the older shape for a short window.

owen: request: include a short prose upgrade note in the API docs and a small example for incremental JSON reassembly. e.g. include this snippet in docs:
```json
{ \"event_type\": \"delta\", \"seq\": 42, \"chunk_index\": 0, \"chunk_count\": 3, \"payload\": { \"content\": \"{\\\"arg\\\":\"pa\"}\" } }
{ \"event_type\": \"delta\", \"seq\": 42, \"chunk_index\": 1, \"chunk_count\": 3, \"payload\": { \"content\": \"rt\\\" } }
{ \"event_type\": \"delta\", \"seq\": 42, \"chunk_index\": 2, \"chunk_count\": 3, \"payload\": { \"content\": \"tern}\" } }
{ \"event_type\": \"eos\", \"seq\": 42, \"payload\": {} }
```

jing: small schema nit — what about `role` nullability during function arg chunks? we occasionally emit role=null for tool fragments. i'd prefer explicit `role: \"tool\"` and `tool_name` in payload so clients don't need to special-case null.

sam: agreed, explicit is easier. also add a tiny telemetry flag `stream_protocol_version` in the initial handshake event so we can iterate without breaking parity.

alex: updated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/12345 — requesting reviews from @owen @maria @jing. added unit tests for seq-based reassembly. deploy-bot: created PR 12345 by alex

deploy-bot: PR #12345 opened in repo redwood/streaming-schema by alex — reviewers requested: owen, maria, jing

owen: i'll take it tonight, if nothing major i'll approve. add the docs example and a simple curl streaming example showing client-side reassembly.

maria: i can check the docs example midday. one more ask: mention the fallback behavior (if seq absent, client should fall back to concatenation by arrival order).

alex: good call — added fallback guidance in the PR description. thanks all :rocket: 

sam: lgtm for the high-level shape. i'll look at function-call chunk handling specifically.

jing: thanks — this should make the reassembly story much simpler for SDKs. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks everyone — keeping this short. will merge after reviews and add the upgrade note in the console release notes.

maria: :white_check_mark:

sam: :+1:
